new_commodity_proposals.evidence: The vocabulary's Egg Noodles [egg-noodles] is a DRY shelf-stable product; this is the refrigerated Asian noodle (Twin Marquis style lo mein or wonton) from the cold case. It flips on both estate tests: a different price class (a 1 lb refrigerated pack runs roughly twice the per-pound price of dry egg noodles) and a different gram basis, 150 g fresh being about 75 g dry. rice-noodles and no-boil-lasagna-noodles are different foods; the board's only hit was `eggs`, a keyword collision.

Rice vinegar and mirin are different foods again.

Board ABSENT. The dried pod of Illicium verum, sold whole in the spice or Asian aisle - NOT the anise seed the FDC shelf returned (Pimpinella anisum, a different plant). No existing spice id covers a whole-pod spice this could hide under.

registrar_rulings.reason: Same food as egg-noodles ($0.1088/oz dry, 7 stores) but a DIFFERENT PURCHASE: refrigerated cold-case pack at ~2x the per-lb price and a different gram basis (150 g fresh ~ 75 g dry), so pricing it under egg-noodles misprices every recipe line; verified no lo-mein/wonton/fresh-pasta id exists anywhere (the only 'lo mein' string in commodities is buckwheat-soba-noodles' OWN exclude, and the board's lo-mein hits are recipe names, not commodities). COLLISION IS LIVE: egg-noodles' include 'egg\s+noodles?' matches fresh-pack product names today and its excludes (ramen, frozen, chow mein) do not fence fresh/refrigerated/lo mein/wonton - the companion edit below is mandatory or two ids claim one product.

Estate genuinely absent: grepped shaoxing/shao hsing/sherry/cooking wine/rice wine across all three namespaces and the feed - zero hits except red-wine's exclude list, which fences sherry OUT (proof the wine ids are deliberately drinking-wine-only). white-wine ($0.1561/floz) prices drinking wine at $6-12/750ml; Shaoxing is a salted Asian-aisle cooking wine at ~$3-4/750ml, so an alias publishes a wrong price in either direction. mirin is a different food (sweet, near-syrup); rice-vinegar is vinegar. Same-form near rows exist but none is the same purchase.

Grepped 'anise' across commodities, recipe-commodities, the recipe board and the live feed: zero hits - the food exists under no name and no price cell. The FDC shelf's anise seed is Pimpinella anisum, a different plant, and five-spice-powder ($4.75/oz, include 'five\s*spice') is a BLEND that merely contains star anise - a different purchase, not a variant. Verified five-spice-powder's excludes carry no anise fence, so cloning its spice-aisle armour is safe.

join_fallbacks: '1 chicken breast ((up to 300g/10 oz))': the qty engine could not ground this weight (count/each guess of 200 g against a line stating 300 g - the engine did not read the stated weight), so its number is a fallback and the cross-check is skipped; recorded to the density gaps list
macro_cross_check: PASSES THE BAND, and only after a corrected each-weight. With chicken at the source's stated 300 g and the noodles on a hydrated basis, per serving at 2 servings: 365 cal, 43.7 g protein, 34.5 g carbs, against the source's published 357 / 41.6 / 33.8 - agreement within 2%, 5% and 2%. Band: 350-650 cal ok, protein >= 40 ok, carbs <= 35 ok but TIGHT at 34.5. Now the catch this check exists for: the settled 200 g on 'up to 300g/10 oz' gives 306 cal and 32.5 g protein per serving, a 22% protein gap against the source and a fail on BOTH the 350 cal floor and the 40 g protein floor - a good dish retired on an each-weight assumption about the main protein. The source's own published macros can only be reached at about 300 g, so I set grams_source 300 and flagged it on the line.
